lastCompletedAction: FOUND-006 ACCEPTED by the owner as locally verified at be2f13e (local technical acceptance only -- not merged, not deployed, no hosted migration, no flag). OF-018 recorded as a separate P2 fail-closed defect and SCHEDULED, deliberately not folded into OF-016 because OF-016's RPCs do not call the affected inbound path. Then built OF-016: the authorized resolution workflow around 0083's existing evidence, with no destructive data migration -- historic pending rows are visible and resolvable as they stand. Migration 0087 adds the `finance.duplicate.resolve` capability, `resolve_duplicate_review` (human-only BY GRANT: authenticated yes, anon and service_role no; actor from auth.uid(); company read from the review row, never from caller input; active membership and capability re-checked under the row locks; state change and audit in one transaction; idempotent on replay, with the standing decision winning a conflicting one), `duplicate_review_queue` (capability checked inside its own predicate), `financial_events.duplicate_of_event_id`, and an immutability trigger that is SECURITY INVOKER on purpose -- a DEFINER version would see its own owner as current_user and wave every writer through, which is the trap FOUND-006 measured and which my first draft fell into until a test that actually exercised the path caught it. The lock order source_events -> financial_events -> duplicate_reviews is documented once and shared with the worker; the source event goes first because claim_source_events takes `for update skip locked` on it, so a reviewer holding it makes the worker SKIP rather than queue behind human review. The subtle part is the resume loop: a dismissal returns the event to draft and re-arms its source event, so without a durable record of the decision the next pass would re-score the same pair and re-pause the payment -- `recentEventsForDedup` now excludes counterparts already ruled distinct FOR THAT EVENT, narrowly, so every other pairing is still scored. UI: /app/finance/duplicate-reviews plus a finance-hub count, an approvals banner (a paused payment has NO approval request, so it can never appear in that list), and a health signal.

openFindings: OF-016: RESOLVED by migration 0087 (pending independent review). The paused payment now has an authorized, audited, idempotent resolution path and a screen; historic 0083 rows work as they stand.

OF-018 (P2, NOT exploitable, recorded not fixed): `resolve_inbound_review` and `record_inbound_review` (0075) guard with `caller_jwt_role() is distinct from 'service_role'` IN ADDITION to their EXECUTE grant. Fail-closed, so not a hole -- but it contradicts the second half of the rule this package enforces: a genuine service_role caller whose claim text differs (a direct connection sets no GUC) is refused. Cheap to correct; belongs in a bounded follow-up.

OF-017 (P1, INHERENT -- not closed by FOUND-006): under the PostgREST shared-login model every API session authenticates as `authenticator`, which Supabase grants membership of both `authenticated` and `service_role`. SET ROLE is authorised against session_user, so a caller with arbitrary SQL as `authenticated` can `set role service_role` and reach every service-only entrypoint. No in-database control can close this while the login role holds both memberships; it requires a separate connection identity for service work, which is an owner infrastructure decision.

OF-014 residual (P1): a caller with arbitrary SQL as the `authenticated` DB role can forge request.jwt.claims — reading one quotation status per id, and more broadly forging `sub` and so auth.uid(). The unauthenticated half is closed. Belongs to FOUND-006.
